title: Mixed conditionals and hypotheses
grammar: Mixed conditionals, I wish / If only

sections.heading: Mixed conditionals
sections.body: Mixed conditionals combine different times in the if clause and the main clause. They are used when the condition and result happen at different times.
table: If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now.
If I were braver, I would have spoken up.

sections.heading: I wish / If only
sections.body: We use 'I wish' and 'If only' to express regrets or desires. The tense depends on whether the regret is about the present or the past.
table: I wish I had more time.
I wish I had studied harder.
I wish it would stop raining.
I wish I could speak French.
If only I knew the answer.
If only I hadn't said that.

sections.heading: Other structures
list: It's time + past simple: It's time we left.
I'd rather + past simple: I'd rather you didn't smoke here.
Suppose / Supposing: Suppose you won the lottery, what would you do?
What if: What if we had taken the other road?

sections.heading: Common mistakes
list: Do not say 'I wish I would have'. Say 'I wish I had'.
Do not use 'will' after 'wish' or 'if only'.
Mixed conditionals combine two times; do not mix tenses randomly.

list.definition: I wish I had taken that job.
It's a shame you couldn't come.
I should have listened to you.
I would have helped if I could.
In your position, I would accept.
If I were you, I would apologise.
In that case, I would say no.
We should leave now, otherwise we will be late.
As a result, we missed the train.
It rained, so we stayed home.
He lied; consequently, no one trusts him.
The road was closed; therefore, we took another route.
Because of this, we changed our plans.

phases.name: Discovery
phases.intro: Look at these sentences. Read them carefully and think about the questions below.
sentences: If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now.
If I were braver, I would have spoken up.
I wish I had more time.
I wish I had studied harder.
If only I hadn't said that.
I wish it would stop raining.
I'd rather you didn't smoke here.
questions: In sentences 1 and 2, which parts of the sentence refer to different times?
In sentences 3 and 4, what is the difference between wishing about the present and the past?
In sentence 5, how does 'if only' change the meaning of the wish?
In sentence 6, what does 'wish + would' express?
In sentences 7 and 8, what other structures express hypothetical situations?

questions.prompt: If I ___ born earlier, I would be retired now.
questions.explanation: Mixed conditional: past condition, present result.

questions.prompt: I wish I ___ how to play the piano.
I wish I ___ studied harder for the exam.
If only I ___ my keys! Now I can't get in.
questions.explanation: Past regret: if only + past perfect.

questions.prompt: If I ___ more money, I would have travelled last year.
questions.explanation: Mixed conditional: past result depends on a past condition.

questions.prompt: It's time we ___ .
I'd rather you ___ tell anyone.
questions.explanation: I'd rather + past simple for present/future wishes.

questions.prompt: If she ___ braver, she would have spoken up.
questions.explanation: Mixed conditional: present condition, past result.

questions.prompt: I wish it ___ raining. I want to go out.
questions.explanation: Wish + would for annoyance or desire for change.

questions.prompt: If only I ___ the answer.
questions.explanation: If only + past simple for present wish.

phases.name: Free practice
prompts: Write 5 sentences with 'I wish' about things you would change in your life (mix past and present).
Write 5 mixed conditional sentences combining past and present (If I had... I would be...).
Write 5 sentences with 'if only' expressing regrets about the past.

questions.prompt: If I ___ known, I would have come.
I wish I ___ taller.
If only I ___ studied medicine. I would be a doctor now.
questions.explanation: Mixed conditional: past condition, present result.

questions.prompt: I wish it ___ sunny tomorrow.
If I ___ you, I would apologise.
I wish I ___ so rude yesterday.
If she ___ harder, she would have passed.
It's time you ___ to bed.
I'd rather you ___ here.
If I ___ braver, I would have asked her out.
questions.explanation: Mixed conditional: present condition, past result.

sections.heading: Key rules
list: Mixed conditionals combine different times: if + past perfect, would + verb (past condition, present result).
If + past simple, would have + pp (present condition, past result).
I wish + past simple: present regret.
I wish + past perfect: past regret.
I wish + would: annoyance or desire for change.
If only: same uses as I wish, but stronger.
It's time + past simple. I'd rather + past simple.

sections.heading: Common mistakes
list: Do not say 'I wish I would have'. Say 'I wish I had'.
Do not use 'will' after 'wish' or 'if only'.
Do not mix tenses randomly in mixed conditionals.

sections.heading: Useful phrases
list: If I had..., I would...
If I were..., I would have...
I wish I...
If only I...
It's time we...
I'd rather you...
